I've just finished a streak of Kunihiko Ikuhara's works. I strated with Yuri Kuma Arashi last season, proceeded to watch Shoujo Kakumei Utena, and concluded things with Mawaru Penguindrum, which is my favorite of the three.

Ikuhara is known for directing very abstract, symbolic experiences. Penguindrum is no different in this regard. As with Utena and Yuri Kuma, Penguindrum is rife with symbolism and deeper meaning, all colluding to ask a deeply existential question at the end. I won't discuss specifics, as piecing things together is half of the fun with Ikuhara's shows, but I find all of the themes that he examines to be incredibly relevant to the human experience. On this alone, I recommend anything this man makes.

It's hard to do justice to the plot's of any of Ikuhara's anime, as they all sound absolutely bizarre sans the deeper meaning. Such is true with Penguindrum. This anime follows the Takakura family, which includes siblings Shouma, Kanba, and Himari. One day, Himari collapses and is taken to the hospital, where she passes away. The brother mourn their dead sister, but soon find that she has been brought back to life by a penguin-themed hat. The hat not only returns Himari to life, but occassionally possesses her body in order to initiate the "Survival Strategy". The Survival Strategy the means by which Himari can be permanently cured of her illness without the help of the hat, and in order to fullfil it, Shouma and Kanba must find the "Penguindrum". Thus, the boys set out on their quest to locate the Penguindrum and save their sister. Along the way, the boys encounter a diverse cast of characters, all with their own pasts and presents. Ikuhara examines the many bonds of these characters and how they affect their actions.

Penguindrum is yet another superbly metaphorical work by Ikuhara. If you enjoy puzzling over the meaning of the many symbols of a show, or just like an insane experience, Mawaru Penguindrum is for you. The show grabs onto your attention and keeps it. You'll watch many of the characters grow according to the fates allotted them, and you'll see them challenge the status quo. Such is what Penguindrum seeks to explore.
